title: Making monsters move randomly in a set area?

posts.author: The_Eerie_One
posts.body: I would like to have two slimes move randomly under a glass display, but I'm having trouble figuring out how. I have the sides of the glass tiles set as impassable so the player can't walk through it, but it makes it so the monsters unable to move within it. I remember reading that events can't move through other events, so I set up some blank events to try and cage them in...but they walked through those so I guess I read that wrong. Any way I can give them random movement and keep them within a specific 6 tile space?

posts.author: SGHarlekin
posts.body:
Could use region restrictions to set the glass boss passable for events, but not the player and similarly around the box use a region that blocks events but not the player.
Events and Movement Core VisuStella MZ - Yanfly.moe Wiki

posts.author: caethyril
posts.body:
By default, an event can only move through another event if at least one of them is marked "Through", because that disables passability checks. (A plugin might change that in some cases, e.g. if I recall correctly Yanfly's Core Engine for MV disables it entirely for some reason. Maybe VisuStella have carried over that behaviour.)
Could you just use
directional passability
for the sides of the glass? That should allow the slimes to move around inside without escaping. The glass itself may be star-passable, but you could put other tiles, either outside the terrarium or layered on top of its glass edges, that are O-passable except in the relevant direction(s).
Another plugin option is
EventMovableLimitation
by triacontane:
RPGMakerMV/EventMovableLimitation.js at mz_master · triacontane/RPGMakerMV

github.com
It does require PluginCommonBase, which ships with RPG Maker MZ under:
<MZ install folder>/dlc/BasicResources/plugins/official/

.js
(Standalone version might be organised differently.)

posts.author: caethyril
posts.body:
In case you're unaware: directional passability is one of the tile data options available on the right-hand side of the Tilesets tab in the database:
You can set certain tiles to be (im)passable only in specific directions. The directional blocks could be something innocuous like carpet trim, or just invisible tiles with specific passability settings~
(Note that directional passability doesn't work if the tile is set to Passage = star, because star means that tile is ignored for passability checks.)
